text: The Patriots are preparing for Sunday's crucial home opener against the Steelers with a mixed injury picture that could significantly impact their offensive firepower: running back TreVeyon Henderson, who missed Week 1 with an ankle injury, declared himself "ready to go" for the contest, but the team faces a major setback with wide receiver A.J. Brown sidelined for approximately four weeks after suffering a high ankle sprain in the opener, forcing other receivers to step up their production in his absence. On the roster front, the Patriots made a practice squad adjustment, signing offensive lineman Xavier Newman-Johnson while releasing Jacob Rizy, minor tweaks that nonetheless reflect the team's ongoing evaluation of depth at the line. Beyond the field, the organization made headlines when owner Robert Kraft explained his decision to have Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming Gillette Stadium shows, citing concerns about what Kraft described as "a history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community." As the Patriots look to secure their first win of 2026 against Pittsburgh, the storylines extend beyond just the game itself, with Friday bringing the emotional return of Hall of Fame cornerback Stephon Gilmore, who will retire as a Patriot during a 2:10 PM press conference at Foxborough.
